classification.difficultyReason: Infer qualitative changes to mean, median and range from added or removed tree heights, including repeated extremes.

inlines.text: State how the summary statistics change using “

spec.description: Three separate unfilled tree outlines on a common baseline, increasing in height from left to right.
spec.mathematics: Three distinct ordered heights. Drawing coordinates express relative appearance only; no numerical heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: The original three trees retain their heights, positions and baseline; a markedly taller fourth tree is added on the right.
spec.mathematics: One new maximum is added. The original minimum and all three original values remain unchanged.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean increases because the added tree is taller than every original tree, so its height is above the original mean.
The median increases. Originally it is the middle height. With four trees, it is the average of the original middle and tallest heights, which is greater.
The range increases because the maximum height increases while the minimum height stays the same.

spec.description: Three separate unfilled trees, increasing in height from left to right on a common baseline.
spec.mathematics: Three distinct ordered heights; no numerical heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: A new shortest tree precedes the unchanged original three trees. All trees share a baseline.
spec.mathematics: One new minimum is added; the original maximum remains unchanged.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean decreases because the added tree is shorter than every original tree, so its height is below the original mean.
The median decreases. The new median is the average of the original shortest and middle heights, which is below the original middle height.
The range increases because the minimum height decreases while the maximum height stays the same.

spec.description: Five trees increase in height from left to right, with the last markedly tallest. All have a common baseline.
spec.mathematics: Five distinct ordered heights; no numerical heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: The original shortest tree is removed. The remaining four trees retain their original positions, heights and baseline.
spec.mathematics: Remove the unique minimum from five distinct ordered heights.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean increases because the removed shortest tree has a height below the original mean.
The median increases from the third original height to the average of the third and fourth original heights.
The range decreases because the minimum height increases while the maximum height stays the same.

spec.description: Five trees increase in height from left to right, with the last markedly tallest. All have a common baseline.
spec.mathematics: Five distinct ordered heights; no numerical heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: The original tallest tree is removed. The four remaining trees retain their original heights, positions and baseline.
spec.mathematics: Remove the unique maximum from five distinct ordered heights.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean decreases because the removed tallest tree has a height above the original mean.
The median decreases from the third original height to the average of the second and third original heights.
The range decreases because the maximum height decreases while the minimum height stays the same.

spec.description: Five trees increase in height from left to right, with the last markedly tallest.
spec.mathematics: Five distinct ordered heights; no numerical heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: Six trees: an added shortest tree on the left followed by the unchanged original five. The two shortest trees use identical geometry and the same baseline.
spec.mathematics: The added value equals the original minimum exactly. Both extremes remain unchanged.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean decreases because the added tree has the minimum height, which is below the original mean.
The median decreases from the third original height to the average of the second and third original heights.
The range does not change. The added tree equals the original shortest tree, so the minimum and maximum heights remain unchanged.

spec.description: Six trees in three ordered pairs: two equal short trees, two equal medium trees and two equal tall trees.
spec.mathematics: Three distinct heights, each repeated twice. Equal heights use identical geometry and a common baseline.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

spec.description: The original six trees are followed by a seventh tree equal to the two original tallest trees. All original geometry and positions are retained.
spec.mathematics: The maximum height now occurs three times. The fourth ordered height remains the medium height.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no answer text.

answer.worked: The mean increases because the added tree has the maximum height, which is above the original mean.
The median does not change. Originally the third and fourth trees have the same medium height, so their average is that height. With seven trees, the fourth tree still has the same medium height.
The range does not change because adding another tree at the existing maximum changes neither the minimum nor the maximum height.
